data.name: Vayunand
data.gender_notes: Vayunand is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vayunand is a powerful Hindu name that represents the god of wind and water, embodying strength and resilience. The name Vayunand carries the meaning “God of Wind and Water” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vayunand usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wind and water and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine power of nature and the balance of elements.
data.etymology: Vayunand belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Wind and Water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vayunand total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Vayunand is a name derived from Hindu mythology that signifies the worship of Vayu, the god of wind, and Varuna, the god of water. In Hinduism, both Vayu and Varuna have been regarded as significant deities since ancient times. The name Vayunand hence embodies the intersection of two essential elements of life - wind and water. It reflects the deep cultural connections of Hinduism with the natural world and the importance of revering the forces of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vayunand holds a deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the unity of the opposing forces of nature - the stability and tranquility associated with water and the dynamism and change brought about by wind. In Hinduism, it is believed that acknowledging and accepting the cyclical nature of these forces and their underlying unity fosters inner peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vayunand signifies the embodiment of the eternal wind or Prana, the vital life force. It represents the constant movement and transformation in life, symbolizing freedom and liberation from material attachments.

vedic_reference.note: Not found in Vedas or Upanishads.

historical_references.reference: The god Vayu was equated with the north wind and was one of the eight Vasus. He was also identified as the king of the winds. In Hindu mythology, Vayu was believed to be the father of Hanuman, the monkey god and the devoted servant of Lord Rama.

Vayunand was mentioned in the 14th century South Indian inscription of the Madurai Nayak rulers, as a title of the king. The inscription refers to a grant made by Maravarman Kulasekhara Koyil Tondaiman, where he is referred to as the 'lord of the winds' or Vayunand.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Vayunand continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Arjun Vayunand, a teacher in Kolkata, India, shares that their name Vayunand meaning "God of Wind and Water" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
